info.title: EcoOps API
info.description:
Enterprise facility management API for Construction & Demolition (C&D) recycling operations.

## Available Modules

| Module | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Production** | Daily crusher output tracking with CDW/RAW feed modes |
| **Dispatch** | Material shipment records with trip counts and owners |
| **Received** | CDW and raw material intake logging |
| **Equipment** | Operational hours and counts per equipment type |
| **Manpower** | Shift-based attendance by role |
| **Inventory** | Auto-calculated from production/dispatch transactions |
| **Actions** | Action management with reminders and OTP-secured updates |
| **Exports** | Job queue-based exports (CSV, Excel, PDF) |
| **Imports** | Bulk CSV/Excel upload with validation |

## Resources

- **OpenAPI Spec (JSON):** [/api/docs/openapi.json](/api/docs/openapi.json)
- **OpenAPI Spec (YAML):** [/api/docs/openapi.yaml](/api/docs/openapi.yaml)


## Authentication

The EcoOps API uses **Bearer Token** authentication. All API requests (except public endpoints) require a valid token in the Authorization header.

> **ℹ️ Note:** Tokens are issued via Better Auth and expire after 7 days of inactivity. Active tokens are automatically extended on each use.

### Step 1: Sign In to Get Token

Make a POST request to the sign-in endpoint. The token is returned in the **response header** `set-auth-token`:

```bash
curl -i -X POST /api/auth/sign-in/email \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "your-email@example.com",
    "password": "your-password"
  }'
```

**Response Headers:**
```
set-auth-token: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
```

**Response Body:**
```json
{
  "user": {
    "id": "user-id",
    "email": "your-email@example.com",
    "name": "Your Name"
  },
  "session": {
    "id": "session-id",
    "expiresAt": "2025-01-14T12:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

### Step 2: Verify Your Token

Test that your token is working by fetching your permissions:

```bash
curl /api/users/me/permissions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
```

**Expected Response:**
```json
{
  "role": "ADMIN",
  "permissions": ["VIEW_PRODUCTION", "INPUT_PRODUCTION", ...],
  "siteAccess": [{"siteId": "JED_01", "canView": true, ...}]
}
```

### Step 3: Use Token in API Calls

Include the token in the Authorization header for all subsequent requests:

```bash
curl /api/production?siteId=JED_01&dateFrom=2025-01-01&dateTo=2025-01-31 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

> **⚠️ Warning:** Extract the token from the `set-auth-token` response header and store it securely. Never expose tokens in client-side code or version control.

### Token Expiration

- Tokens expire after **7 days** of inactivity
- Active tokens are automatically extended for another 7 days on each use
- When a token expires, generate a new one by signing in again

### Public Endpoints

> **✅ Tip:** The following endpoints do not require authentication:

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `/api/auth/*` | Authentication endpoints |
| `/api/docs` | API documentation |
| `/api/health` | Health check |
| `/api/actions/public/*` | Public action tracker updates (OTP-secured) |
